question: Should core expose an agent-facing capacity projection, and should it include caller-visible per-agent workload or only anonymous lane aggregates?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the implementation seam but cannot choose the durable model-facing visibility, privacy, and scheduling semantics; current session tools deliberately scope information to the caller.

options.title: Expose scoped capacity
options.body: Return aggregate lane saturation plus workload details only for agents and sessions the caller is already authorized to inspect.

options.title: Expose anonymous aggregates
options.body: Return lane limits, active counts, and queue depths without agent or session identities.

options.title: Keep snapshots operator-only
options.body: Retain caller-scoped agent tools and reserve global queue introspection for human operator surfaces.

recommendation.title: Expose scoped capacity
recommendation.body: Return aggregate lane saturation plus workload details only for agents and sessions the caller is already authorized to inspect.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest combined history signal covers command queues, agent tools, concurrency behavior, and prior review context for this exact issue.
